items.title: Neutral Go oracle, API inventory and fixture harness
items.stop_rule: No Rust production crate until Go↔Go self-equality, source-digest rejection, isolated side effects and a deliberate negative-control failure are proven.

items.title: Pinned Rust workspace and contracts/foundation slice
items.stop_rule: Do not accept changed bytes, paths, errors or defaults because Rust/framework conventions differ.

items.title: Filesystem and secret-reference safety slice
acceptance_commands: MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-disable-isolation cargo +nightly miri test -p symaira-core-fs -p symaira-core-secretref --all-features
items.stop_rule: Stop on weaker symlink/race/path protection, secret disclosure, extra runtime coupling or owned unsafe code without an approved ADR.

items.title: MCP stdio and typed-tool feasibility slice
items.stop_rule: Use an owned raw adapter when rmcp defaults differ; never change framing, tool errors, schema bytes or stdout purity to fit the SDK.

items.title: Foundation multi-consumer adoption and value gate
items.stop_rule: Stop or shrink the Rust foundation if it lacks two adopters/two-language ownership, fails to remove duplication, breaks standalone-first or exceeds the 10% representative regression ceiling.

items.title: SQLite open, pragma, migration and locking slice
items.stop_rule: Keep deferred until two Rust consumers need the same SQLite policy. Do not claim parity from SQL text alone; stop on DB bytes/schema/pragmas/locking/rollback drift or unacceptable bundled-SQLite cost.

items.title: Update, archive, Cosign and atomic apply slice
items.stop_rule: Do not mark complete until UPD-001..012 have executable Go/Rust parity and native evidence on every required target. Stop on redirect/TLS weakening, traversal/symlink writes, checksum-byte drift, broken rollback or replacement of a known-good binary.

items.title: Descriptor-driven LLM provider slice
items.stop_rule: Do not duplicate provider wire transports in consumers or create a Rust ollamakit clone. Chat/stream cancellation and async transport injection are implemented; keep the item in progress while remaining per-operation cancellation and parity evidence are open. Consumer adapters retain product policy and exact Git pins. Stop on credential leakage, redirect drift, streaming/tool-wire drift or taxonomy changes.

items.title: Audit and grounded-evidence algorithm slices
items.stop_rule: Terminal shared-library decision: implement and verify in the linked consumer, not a shared CoreKit crate. Retain the Go package until its last released importer is removed; reassess only when two independent consumers need matching semantics. Stop on hash/JSONL/offset/tie-breaking drift.

items.title: MCP configuration discovery slice
items.stop_rule: Keep blocked until second-consumer demand; do not generalize platform paths or silently normalize malformed client configs.

items.title: DOM selection and rendering feasibility slice
items.stop_rule: Terminal shared-library decision: implement and verify in the linked consumer, not a shared CoreKit crate. Retain the Go package until its last released importer is removed; reassess only when two independent consumers need matching semantics. Select no parser/renderer until the full corpus passes; do not normalize unexplained Markdown bytes.

items.title: TurboQuant codec and performance slice
items.stop_rule: Terminal shared-library decision: implement and verify in the linked consumer, not a shared CoreKit crate. Retain the Go package until its last released importer is removed; reassess only when two independent consumers need matching semantics. Persisted sidecar/bit bytes stay immutable; p95/throughput may not regress by more than 10%.

items.title: Full dual-language hardening and native CI
items.stop_rule: No crate proceeds with untriaged advisories/licenses, missing native runtime proof, unfuzzed untrusted parsers or broken Go gates.

items.title: Released Git-pinned consumers and standalone/rollback evidence
items.stop_rule: Before any crates.io publication, each recorded consumer must have a real public release of its exact Git-pinned Rust snapshot, source-bound standalone/rollback reports, artifact and report digests, and independent release-artifact readback. A local tag or verifier pass alone is insufficient; retain Go support.

items.title: SemVer, publishing manifest and release verification
items.stop_rule: Do not publish before RUST-016 release and artifact evidence, required migration/native/security gates and a separate release approval. Publish only adopted crates with explicit versions/order/provenance and external registry read-back; repository tags must remain unambiguous for Go consumers.

items.title: Registry-pinned consumer rollout and Go-retention review
items.stop_rule: Do not pass this gate without new releases pinned to exact registry versions and verified lockfiles/artifacts. No Go package removal while a released consumer imports it; retirement is a separate major-version decision with a tested rollback.

items.title: Consumer-used API closure and versioned adapters
items.stop_rule: Stop on unmapped consumer API, unversioned drift, skipped/zero-case/native-missing evidence, weakened filesystem/TLS policy, unbounded cancellation or missing rollback. Mapping alone does not authorize consumer cutover.
